subject: Operations
title: Biological Manufacturing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Biological Manufacturing.

hook.text: A company grows leather from cells in a lab—no cows, no ranches, no deforestation. Biology is becoming a factory.

buildup.text: Biological manufacturing uses engineered organisms—bacteria, yeast, algae—to produce materials, chemicals, and food.

discovery.text: It can create spider silk, biodegradable plastics, and lab-grown meat without traditional agricultural supply chains.

twist.text: Scaling biological processes from lab to factory is enormously hard. Biology is unpredictable at industrial volumes.

climax.text: Bolt Threads and Ginkgo Bioworks are building the factories and platforms for biology-based manufacturing.

punchline.text: The factory of the future might be alive.

quiz.question: What is biological manufacturing?
options: Using engineered organisms to produce materials
